key_insight: Leading LLMs can generate varied colonoscopy-prep conversations, but response correctness and safety vary enough that automated screening and deferral may be needed.
clinical_relevance: Conversational AI could help patients understand bowel-prep instructions and answer routine questions, potentially improving procedure readiness while reducing avoidable cancellations.
method: Generated 250 synthetic patient–AI coach dialogues per model with 3–7 question-answer pairs each.
Compared five LLMs on correctness, harmfulness, and diversity using human expert review plus LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.
Tested a safety filter that replaced incorrect answers with a deferral advising patients to contact their healthcare provider.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports human and automated evaluation of 250 dialogues per model, with model-to-model correctness differences tested by permutation analysis and inter-rater reliability measured using Gwet’s AC1.
watch_item: Synthetic dialogue quality does not guarantee real-world clinical reliability, and deferral-only safeguards may still leave gaps for patient-specific prep questions.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
